title: Chapter VIII · That the hiding of grace for a time works together for our good

blocks.s: 9. But do not be afraid, O bride; do not despair, do not think yourself despised, if the Bridegroom withdraws his face from you for a little while. All these things work together for your good, and you gain both from his coming and from his going. He comes for you, and for you he also withdraws. He comes for consolation; he withdraws as a precaution, lest the greatness of the consolation puff you up; lest, if the Bridegroom were always with you, you should begin to despise your companions and attribute this continual visitation no longer to grace but to nature. But this grace the Bridegroom gives to whom he will and when he will; it is not possessed as if by right of inheritance. It is a common proverb that too much familiarity breeds contempt. So he withdraws, lest perhaps by being too constant he be despised, and so that being absent he may be more desired, being desired he may be sought more eagerly, and being long sought he may at last be found with more thanks. Besides, if this consolation, which compared with the glory to come that will be revealed in us is dark and partial, were never lacking here, we might perhaps think we had here a lasting city and seek the one to come the less. So let us not take exile for our homeland, nor the pledge for the full price. The Bridegroom comes, and in turn withdraws; now bringing consolation, now turning our whole bed into weakness. For a little while he lets us taste how sweet he is, and before we feel it fully he withdraws himself: and so, hovering over us as if with wings spread, he provokes us to fly. As if he said: See, you have tasted a little how sweet and pleasant I am; but if you want to be filled full of this sweetness, run after me in the fragrance of my ointments, with your hearts lifted up, where I am at the right hand of God the Father. There you shall see me, not through a glass in a dark manner, but face to face; and your heart shall rejoice fully, and your joy no one shall take from you.
